behavioralConstraints: run() validates trimmed non-empty ownerId/runId/idempotencyKey, RFC 3339 occurredAt, bounded retry policy, and optional integer timeoutMs in 1..2147483647 before any wrapped stage; an invalid request is INVALID_REQUEST
idempotencyKey defaults to runId; the journal binds the key to one ownerId/runId and original occurredAt; a different owner/run under the key is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT

the local run store atomically replaces the journal and holds a non-stealing repository-wide exclusive lock across the whole async run; competing same-key or different-key invocations cannot execute concurrently
a fresh bound task/start result comes from DeveloperStartWorkflow.start(); resumes use the bound task and read authoritative lifecycleState.get rather than infer progress from journal stage summaries
IN_DEVELOPMENT invokes or reuses the Developer provider result before DeveloperValidationGate.validate(); the Developer agent outcome is traceability only and never overrides deterministic validation
DEV_VALIDATION_FAILED returns STOPPED at dev-validation and never invokes review rework or later review stages; there is no automated lifecycle recovery from this state

only task.requiredReviewRoles stages at valid persisted lifecycle entry states run; each role uses its own gate prepareContext output and submits its provider outcome/findings/details/evidenceRefs/nonPass unchanged
cached provider output is reused only for the same task, role, exact revision, actor and context content identity; mismatch is RECOVERY_REQUIRED rather than stale judgment replay
review submission preserves the provider result runId and occurredAt, making the same logical submission an exact ReviewFramework retry rather than a new evidence record

a non-PASS QA/Architecture/UAT result, including a previously persisted failed lifecycle state on resume, routes through ReviewReworkGate.enterRework and returns STOPPED; REWORK_REQUIRED stays stopped pending explicit rework
merge-readiness ready:false returns STOPPED and may be re-evaluated on same-key resume; with no pending controlled-merge intent, a fresh merge call requires a preceding ready:true result

pending controlled-merge intent or lifecycle MERGED/DONE delegates directly to BOOT-025 without a preliminary open-PR readiness query; BOOT-025 owns exact-head verification, remote merge confirmation and completion bookkeeping
COMPLETED is returned through ControlledMergeController confirmed DONE only; the engine never performs the merge HTTP call itself
every stage summary and provider invocation uses a stable derived identity ${request.runId}::<stage-id>; retrying a provider stage does not create another role identity
retryPolicy defaults to maxAttempts=3, delayMs=100; maxAttempts must be an integer 1..10 including the first attempt; delayMs must be an integer 0..60000

provider attempt counts are persisted before invocation per stage/key and survive restarts/resumes; only actual recoverable AgentProviderError TIMEOUT or PROVIDER_ERROR automatically retries with a fixed abortable delay

provider CANCELLED, malformed results, unsupported roles, context mismatch, preconditions, and mutating-gate failures are not automatically retried; semantic review/validation FAIL or BLOCKED is never retryable infrastructure
the final failed provider attempt propagates its typed error; a later resume without remaining budget throws RETRY_EXHAUSTED; explicit policy increases remain bounded by 10 total attempts

overall request timeout and caller abort compose a signal passed to AgentRunner; timeoutMsFor(role) independently supplies per-attempt provider timeout; CANCELLED and overall TIMEOUT remain distinct errors
cancellation and deadlines are cooperative at gate boundaries: active mutating gates drain while exclusivity is held; no rollback is implied and no overlapping recovery begins before settlement

default actor identity is ownerId for Developer and ${ownerId}::${role} otherwise; default tool policy is allowedTools=[] and networkAccess=none; caller hooks must preserve stable identity and role separation across resumes
journal stage summaries contain at most one entry per stage in ORCHESTRATION_STAGE_IDS order and can refresh on resume; they are not an append-only retry history or authoritative evidence

createLocalOrchestrationEngine composes existing local gates, reads the existing lifecycle store and adds a FileOrchestrationRunStore under .agent/state/orchestration; no direct lifecycle mutation or evidence write occurs in this module

an abrupt process death can retain the lock; operators must stop and verify all repository runners, inspect and remove only the verified stale orchestration lock, retain the journal, and resume the same key/owner/run; no automatic time/PID lock stealing or general state repair is provided

2.0.0 requires custom constructors to supply durable runStore and read-only lifecycleState; BOOT-027 in-flight runs without journals and corrupted state are not automatically migrated or reconstructed
a runId cannot be rebound to a different idempotency key; retry counts cannot decrease and completed start/provider checkpoints cannot be replaced or erased
FileOrchestrationRunStore uses SHA-256-key .run.json files and .orchestration.lock; same-directory temporary write, file fsync, atomic rename and directory fsync precede a successful save

journal reads return detached snapshots; writes require the owning withLock callback and lock token; malformed, non-JSON, oversized over 16 Mi-character, wrong-identity or symlinked journal paths fail closed

IN_DEVELOPMENT resume calls DeveloperStart with expectedTaskId to revalidate the existing bound assignment/branch/context before provider or validation; mismatched task/branch/lock fails RECOVERY_REQUIRED and cannot select new work

an incomplete Developer provider run with changed refreshed revision/context fails RECOVERY_REQUIRED; a completed cached Developer result is retained only for traceability and not rerun, while BOOT-016 validates the actual current canonical revision
invariants: authoritative lifecycle and recorded evidence outrank journal summaries or provider narrative; this engine never calls transitionLifecycle or writes authoritative evidence
failed/blocked required gates remain semantic stops, never automatic infrastructure retries or fabricated successes
role contexts remain exact gate-produced packages; default actor IDs remain separate from Developer, and concrete provider policy remains injected
completed authoritative transitions are skipped on resume; controlled merge owns any remote merge and all merge/completion recovery
journal identity and durable bounded attempts are preserved across retries and process restarts
a cancellation does not release exclusivity while a mutating gate remains active; provider cancellation requires adapter cooperation for remote side effects
no concrete AI vendor SDK, distributed scheduler, or fantasy product behavior is introduced
examples: a provider TIMEOUT followed by PASS uses two durable attempts with one stable stage runId and only one exact review submission
a QA FAIL records evidence, enters REWORK_REQUIRED and stops before Architecture/UAT without automatically retrying the judgment
cancellation during QA aborts the provider signal; its late result cannot advance a gate; an explicit same-key resume consults durable lifecycle and remaining budget
a concurrent duplicate key is rejected by the repository lock; a later same-key resume does not duplicate completed transitions or merge
a remotely confirmed merge interrupted before local completion resumes from persisted controlled-merge intent through BOOT-025 even when the PR has already closed
a readiness STOPPED result can become COMPLETED after CI or PR blockers are resolved and the same request is resumed
edgeCases: a cached result with changed revision/context/actor is rejected as RECOVERY_REQUIRED, even if its outcome was PASS
a journal for a missing or mismatched task lifecycle cannot establish permission to replay a stage
a Developer FAIL/BLOCKED agent result still proceeds to deterministic validation; a validation failure does not use the review-rework path
tasks omitting QA or Architecture do not invoke those provider/review stages; gates still own all resulting lifecycle transitions
a restart cannot reset exhausted provider attempts; merely attaching code=TIMEOUT to an arbitrary error does not make it automatically retryable
an uncooperative provider can continue external work after runner rejection; adapters must respect abort and deduplicate side effects by stable task/role/revision/run identity
a crash between authoritative gate persistence and journal summary update may omit that summary; durable lifecycle still prevents replay of completed transitions
a stale lock is deliberately not stolen from an uncertain live writer; memory run stores provide no process-restart durability
Developer can change HEAD during implementation; its already-cached result is not approval of that HEAD and deterministic validation still reads the actual revision

forbiddenDependencies: direct lifecycle transitions or evidence writes
assignment or branch mutation outside owning gates

expectations: preserve idempotencyKey/ownerId/runId across explicit resumes and expose bounded-attempt exhaustion, conflicts, cancellation and recovery errors

cooperative cancellation may wait for an active mutating gate; concrete providers must honor abort and stable run identity

requiredReachableRanges: COMPLETED for a fully passing merge-ready workflow
STOPPED independently at dev-validation, qa-review, architecture-review, uat-review and merge-readiness
same-key resume without duplicate completed transitions or remote merge

journal attempt/failure metadata describe execution and cannot constitute review approval
acceptedRanges: ordered possibly non-contiguous OrchestrationStageRecord[] with at most one entry per stage
durable attempt counts and last-failure diagnostics including infrastructure, cancellation and preconditions

gate-generated context and stable stage identity flow unchanged into manual packets
imported transport result is handled only through existing runner and authoritative workflow gates
same-key explicit resume retains lifecycle checks and durable budgets; local pending timeout differs from immutable external failure
acceptedRanges: typed provider, workflow and run-store errors
requiredReachableRanges: pending provider interruption and safe explicit same-key resume
deterministic validation of actual HEAD after a Developer implementation changes it
